q: Matter is used to cover all the substances and materials from which the _____ is composed.
e: Matter is used to cover all the substances and materials from which the physical universe is composed.

q: Nowadays, there is a fourth state of matter known as _____ which is a hot ionised gas containing charged particles.
e: Plasma is a hot ionised gas containing charged particles, representing the fourth state of matter.

q: The particles in a solid are packed very tightly together with _____ forces between one another.
e: The particles in a solid are packed very tightly together with strong forces between one another.

q: Solids have a definite _____ and volume.
e: Solids have a definite shape and volume due to the strong forces holding their particles in fixed positions.

q: Liquids can have a definite volume, because the particles in liquid are held together _____ than those in gases.
e: Liquids can have a definite volume, because the particles in liquid are held together more strongly than those in gases.

q: The particles in a gas are in constant and rapid motion because of _____ attractive forces between gaseous particles.
e: The particles in a gas are in constant and rapid motion because of weak attractive forces between gaseous particles.

q: Brownian motion is the continuous random movement of small particles suspended in a gas or liquid, which arises from _____ with the gas or liquid particles.
e: Brownian motion arises from collisions with the gas or liquid particles, causing continuous random movement.

q: In diffusion, the particles of one substance mix with and move through the particles of _____ substance.
e: In diffusion, the particles of one substance mix with and move through the particles of another substance.

q: The speed of diffusion of particles is affected by the mass of particles and by the _____.
e: The speed of diffusion of particles is affected by the mass of particles and by the temperature.

q: The bigger the mass, the _____ the particles diffuse.
e: The bigger the mass, the slower the particles diffuse.

q: The smaller the mass, the _____ the particles diffuse.
e: The smaller the mass, the faster the particles diffuse.

q: The higher the temperature, it enables the particles to diffuse _____.
e: The higher the temperature, it enables the particles to diffuse faster.

q: Unlike gases, solids cannot be compressed and do not _____.
e: Unlike gases, solids cannot be compressed and do not flow.

q: Solids do expand _____ when heated.
e: Solids do expand slightly when heated.

q: Liquids can take up the shape of the container because particles are able to move _____ throughout the liquids.
e: Liquids can take up the shape of the container because particles are able to move freely throughout the liquids.

q: The gas in a container spreads out to occupy the whole space of the container taking its shape and _____.
e: The gas in a container spreads out to occupy the whole space of the container taking its shape and volume.

q: Diffusion is mainly seen in _____ and gases.
e: Diffusion is mainly seen in liquids and gases.

q: Plasma is a hot _____ gas containing charged particles.
e: Plasma is a hot ionised gas containing charged particles.

q: When a few drops of perfume are released into a room, the particles of perfume move through the air and _____ the room.
e: When a few drops of perfume are released into a room, the particles of perfume move through the air and spread the room.

q: Preparing tea using a tea bag in hot water is an example of _____ in daily life.
e: Preparing tea using a tea bag in hot water is an example of diffusion of particles.

q: The motion of pollen grains on still water is an example of _____ motion.
e: The motion of pollen grains on still water is an example of Brownian motion.

q: Mercury and bromine are examples of elements that are _____ at room temperature.
e: Some elements are liquids, such as mercury and bromine.

q: Oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen and chlorine are examples of elements that are _____ at room temperature.
e: Some elements are gases such as oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen and chlorine.

q: Copper, iron, zinc, silver, gold, carbon and phosphorus are examples of elements that are _____ at room temperature.
e: Some elements are solids such as copper, iron, zinc, silver, gold, carbon and phosphorus.

q: Metals have _____ density compared to non-metals.
e: Metals have high density, whereas non-metals have low density.
